analysis.title: USA: Job Openings and Factory Orders Above Expectations
key_insights: JOLTS job openings rose 333k to 7,523k in September from an upwardly revised August level of 7,190k (revised up 111k), above the median forecast of 7,164k and GS's 7,200k.
Openings rose most in professional and business services (+106k) and manufacturing (+54k). State and local government openings rose 108k, likely reflecting hiring tied to the US midterm elections.
The hiring rate rose 0.1pp to 3.4% and the quits rate rose 0.2pp to 2.1%. The layoff rate fell 0.1pp to 1.0%.
GS's jobs-workers gap, built from JOLTS, Indeed and LinkUp job openings measures, has rebounded over the year to 0.3mn in October from -0.5mn in January.

Factory orders rose 1.8% MoM in September, above the median forecast of +1.2% and GS's +0.7%. Orders excluding transportation rose 1.3%, driven by continued strength in machinery orders and modest growth in almost all other durable goods categories.
August core capital goods orders growth was revised up 0.1pp to +0.6%. Core capital goods shipments and durable goods ex-transportation were left unrevised for August.
GS left its Q4 GDP tracking estimate unchanged at +1.8% quarter-over-quarter annualized and raised its past-quarter (Q3) GDP tracking estimate by 0.1pp to +3.5%.

charts_described: The report includes a chart of measures of job openings (JOLTS, Indeed, LinkUp and their average, 2020-2026) and a chart of the US jobs-workers gap based on those measures (2018-2026). The text gives no values for either beyond the 0.3mn October and -0.5mn January gap estimates. A third chart shows core capex orders as a 6-month annualized % change (2015-2025), with no values described.
